subject: Urgent: sustained latency & errors on reserved pool — immediate assistance requested
messages:
From: Alicia Dominguez <alicia.dominguez@helixbank.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@helixbank.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sustained latency + errors on reserved pool (urgent)

Hi Chloe,

We started seeing a persistent increase in tail latency and a spike in 5xx errors against our reserved capacity this morning (from ~08:30 PST). Our pipeline uses the reserved pool you provisioned under DEAL-9821; we're now seeing request timeouts and throughput drops that are impacting production. I've attached a latency snapshot and a short CSV of request distribution.

Key impacts:
- 99th percentile latency up from 180ms to ~1.8s since 08:45
- Error rate for `generate` calls increased to ~2.3% for a 30m window
- Throughput falling below our contracted baseline at peak times, causing backpressure in our job-workers

We need an ops bridge and an immediate mitigation plan. Can you help us prioritize this and confirm whether this is saturation of the dedicated GPU pool or a platform-side regression? We're happy to jump on a 30min call now.

Thanks,
Alicia Dominguez
Senior Engineering Manager, Helix Bank
Alicia.Dominguez@helixbank.com

Hi Alicia — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. I'm on it.

Immediate plan:
- Kick off a short ops bridge (I can start a 30-min call in 10 minutes)
- Internal triage with infra + serving runtime to confirm whether this is pool saturation or a model/kernel level regression
- If saturation, we'll apply temporary throttles and route non-production traffic to avoid noisy neighbors while we stabilize

I'm cc'ing our capacity lead (karthik), runtime lead (jonas) and account lead (naomi) to coordinate. We'll follow up on the bridge with concrete mitigations and an ETA for when throughput returns to baseline.

Call invite: 30-minute bridge scheduled — joining link in follow-up calendar invite.

—Chloe

Subject: Re: Sustained latency + errors on reserved pool (urgent)

Chloe / team — quick triage notes (observed in our metrics):

- Timeline: spike begins ~2027-03-14 08:42 PST, peaked at 09:00–09:10 with queue depth growth on pool `reserved-de-9821`
- Root cause signal: sustained high concurrent batch requests from Helix's ingestion workers; those jobs bypassed burst controls and pushed concurrent RPS beyond the pool allocation
- Impact: scheduler queueing + GPU kernel contention -> long tails and occasional OOM-induced 5xxs

Short-term mitigations (we should apply these ASAP):
1) Enforce per-client burst throttle to cap concurrent requests to contract baseline (we can push a config change now)
2) Route Helix to a reserved fallback pool with slightly higher headroom while we investigate (requires a quick config flip)
3) Enable a temporary model-variant downgrade (quantized fp16) for non-sensitive flows to reduce token cost and kernel contention

I've attached a PNG of pool metrics for the 2-hr window. If Sales wants to avoid churn, we should be prepared to offer a limited SLA credit while we remediate. Marking for Marissa for commercial guidance.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Capacity & Reliability — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sustained latency + errors on reserved pool (urgent)

Chloe / Karthik — adding technical detail from serving runtime: 

- Observed high KV cache churn and kernel scheduling delays coincident with the spike window (08:45–09:15). This aligns with increased long-context requests from Helix's fraud-detector pipeline.
- 5xxs correlate with temporary OOMs on one of the shard hosts; that host's OOM logs point to a sequence-length distribution shift that wasn't captured by the current kernel selection profile.

Recommendation:
- Immediate: route traffic to a low-latency quantized variant of the model to reduce memory pressure (as Karthik suggested)
- Medium-term: create a reserved isolated pool for Helix to prevent noisy-neighbor impact (needs coordination with Sales and Capacity, can be provisioned within 24–36 hours)

Quote from logs: "[2027-03-14T08:56:32Z] kernel_select: fallback due to max_seq > tuned_seq -> increased allocation"

I'll stand by on the bridge to walk through logs.

—Jonas

1) Customer experience: Helix is in production; mitigate now and get us to a 48-hour stabilization window. If we can make them whole quickly we'll avoid an executive ping. Offer: 10% invoice credit for impacted window and a prioritized migration to an isolated reserved pool.

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Next steps / summary — Helix reserved pool incident (action items & timeline)

Hi Alicia — thank you again for your patience on the bridge earlier today. Below is a concise summary and immediate actions we've taken: 

What we saw: sustained headroom pressure on your reserved pool starting 2027-03-14 08:42 PST; this caused kernel fallback and occasional OOMs yielding higher tails and a small number of 5xxs.

Actions completed (immediate):
- Temporary per-client burst throttle applied to align to contracted baseline (went live 2027-03-14 10:10 PST)
- Short-term routing to a higher-headroom fallback pool (config flip completed 2027-03-14 11:00 PST)
- Non-sensitive flows moved to a quantized variant to reduce memory pressure (applied 2027-03-14 11:12 PST)

Planned (next 24–72 hours):
- Provision an isolated reserved pool for Helix (capacity team will provision within 24–36 hrs; Karthik leading)
- Draft SLA addendum (attached) for burst/credit terms and DocuSign link to follow
- Post-mortem & kernel-selection tune to capture Helix's sequence-length distribution (Jonas leading)

Commercial: Marissa has proposed a 10% invoice credit for the impacted window; we'll finalize once the scope is confirmed.

We appreciate the urgency and will keep you updated hourly on the provisioning and remediation timeline. If you prefer, we can schedule a follow-up exec sync with our CTO/CRO — please let me know.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
